newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram to return as finance minister.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram to return as finance minister.

text.p: Former finance minister P. Chidambaram will return to his post in the new government of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral, but the swearing-in ceremony has been postponed, officials said on Wednesday.

Chidambaram, three other members of his regional Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) party, Janata Dal party leader Jaipal Reddy and Maqbool Dar will be inducted into Gujral's council of ministers, a senior government official said.
However, the swearing-in ceremony, originally set for 7:30 p.m. (1400 GMT) on Wednesday, has been postponed and will be rescheduled soon, the official said. No date has yet been set.
The decision to put off the ceremony followed a request by the prospective ministers and did not reflect any hitch in the government's plans, he said.

"There is no problem as such," said the official, who asked not to be identified. "Those who will move into the council of ministers want a particular date and this evening did not suit them. There is no hiccup."
Many Indian politicians commonly consult astrologers before arranging their schedules.
TMC leader G.K. Moopanar announced late on Tuesday in the southern city of Madras that the regional party would enter Gujral's government.
The party tentatively decided on April 19 to stay out of the new government after the ruling United Front passed over Moopanar in its leadership choice.
TMC leaders had left the final decision on whether to join the government to Moopanar, who said it was in the national interest for the party to take ministerial portfolios.

Chidambaram will be renamed finance minister, a post which Gujral has held for himself since assuming power on April 21 in hopes that the economic strategist would return to government, officials said.

Three other TMC leaders were also expected to rejoin the government. M. Arunachalam would return to become labour minister, while S.R. Balasubramaniam would be junior personnel minister and Dhanushkodi Athithan junior human resource development minister.
Newspapers said Jaipal Reddy, longtime spokesman for Gujral's Janata Dal party, was expected to become information and broadcasting minister, replacing C.M. Ibrahim.
The senior government official said Reddy would have a full cabinet post, but possibly not information and broadcasting.
Ibrahim, a close confidant of former prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda, is also in charge of civil aviation.
Maqbool Dar could not take the oath of office on April 21 when the rest of Gujral's team was sworn in. He was expected to become junior home (interior) minister.
